content: Aerosol for Space Treatment The aerosol device for space treatment must include an engine equipped with an easy-start mechanism. Electrically powered units designed for indoor use must adhere to the same standards regarding spray tank capacity and droplet size as other models. For engine-driven cold foggers: The fuel tank must be positioned below the engine. Engine controls, including an engine stop switch, must be mounted in a location visible to the operator. The engine and blower unit should be mounted on a knapsack frame designed for comfortable carrying on the operator's back, with a vibration-dampening system. The knapsack frame must include a non-absorbent padded backrest. All adjustable parts of the equipment must be permanently and clearly marked. The portable cold fogger must meet additional requirements: The fuel tank should have sufficient capacity to allow at least one hour of operation without stopping the engine. The type of fuel and its mixture must be permanently indicated on the fuel tank, filler cap, and machine. The pesticide tank must have a capacity of at least 1 liter and include a clear gauge to indicate the liquid volume. A built-in filter or funnel must be provided unless a ready-to-use container is used. If the tank is pressurized above 50 kPa, a device to fully depressurize the tank before opening must be included. A vortical nozzle must shear the spray into droplets with a volume median diameter (VMD) of less than 30 µm at the recommended output for waterand oil-based formulations. A liquid cut-off valve is required to stop fogging at any time, and the flow of liquid to the nozzle must be controlled by a fixed, interchangeable restrictor or a control valve. Flow rate settings must be marked on the valve or restrictor and listed in the user manual. Durability and Noise Levels The sprayer must operate for a total of 50 hours without failure or restarting issues. Durability tests should be conducted with water using the largest restrictor, with the flow interrupted at 15-minute intervals. Equipment must be labeled to indicate the need for ear protection if noise levels exceed 85 decibels. Noise levels should not exceed 100 decibels at a distance of 3 meters from the machine during operation. Vehicle-Mounted Cold Foggers Vehicle-mounted cold foggers are designed for outdoor space treatments and must meet the following requirements: The equipment must be mounted on a corrosion-resistant frame suitable for a truck, trailer, boat, amphibious vehicle, or drone. A pesticide tank with a capacity of at least 50 liters must be included, along with an additional tank for flushing the system. The fuel tank must have sufficient capacity for at least 2 hours of operation. All tanks must be permanently marked and include drainage facilities. The engine exhaust and moving parts must be guarded to prevent injury. A remote control system in the vehicle cabin must allow operation of the machine and pesticide flow independently, ensuring no pesticide enters the cabin. Manually Carried Thermal Foggers Portable thermal foggers are primarily used for space spray treatments in buildings, houses, and outdoor areas inaccessible to vehicles. These devices must: Include a thermal energy nozzle to meter insecticide liquids (oiland water-miscible formulations). Be equipped with a battery-starting mechanism, a manual or battery-operated air pump for pressurizing the fuel line, and a robust frame for safe handling. Have all hot surfaces adequately guarded to prevent burns. Be labeled with safety instructions warning operators not to leave the fogger unattended during operation. The equipment must operate for 50 hours without failure and must not exceed 85 decibels in noise levels. Aerosol Dispensers for Aircraft Disinfection Aerosolized products for aircraft disinfection are used to control harmful insects. WHO guidelines recommend three techniques: pre-flight, blocks-away, and top-of-descent. Aerosol dispensers must: Be non-refillable and comply with international regulations for air transport. Use non-flammable, non-toxic, and non-irritant formulations that do not damage aircraft materials. Be clearly marked with the percentage of active ingredients, net weight, expiry date, batch number, and safety instructions. The aerosol spray must meet specific physical requirements, including droplet size distribution, and the container must pass heat stability and rough usage tests. This professional summary provides a clear and detailed explanation of the requirements and specifications for fogging and aerosol equipment, ensuring compliance with safety and operational standards.
